design.title: Bigger magnifying glass: the 128 px frame is enlarged in-graph to 288 px instead of 224 px before the EfficientNet-B0 trunks, so Berlin's small structures (cars, roof edges, kerbs, tree crowns) reach the borrowed filters at a scale closer to the one their ImageNet invariance was learned on
design.init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR — unchanged
design.eli5: The drone's camera picture is small, and the pre-trained 'eyes' we borrow were taught on everyday photos where things are big. Last time we blew the picture up to the size those eyes are used to, it was one of the biggest improvements so far. This time we blow it up a bit more, so cars, roof edges and street corners look less like specks and more like the shapes the eyes already know how to recognise in any lighting or season — without adding any memory to the drone.
design.hypothesis: Builds on experiment 15, the one input-scale change of this era and one of its largest single steps: resizing the 128 px frame in-graph to 224 px (the trunk's ImageNet resolution) took held-out truedop_2024 from 65.5% to 74.25% usable (mission 0.395 -> 0.293) with zero new parameters. Its reading was FixRes-style: the pretrained filters carry invariance at the object scales they were trained on, and a 1 m/px aerial frame shows structures far smaller than ImageNet objects (a car is ~4 px at 128, ~7 px at 224). That lever was pulled once and never revisited; every experiment since has kept 224. Meanwhile the remaining gap on the champion (exp 20: 93.0% usable, 0.75% false, 6.25% abstain on truedop_2024; 100%/0% on the three training photographs at the same viewpoints) is the survey gap, and the survey-invariance lever that has paid on this ruler is what the PRETRAINED TRUNK brings (MNV3-S -> MNV2 -> B0), not training-procedure invariance tricks (JS consistency exp 23, continuous vantages exp 22, patchwork exp 27, LP-FT exp 26, Noisy-Student weights exp 25 all failed to beat 0.0777). A bigger trunk is closed by the size gate (31.7 MB of 33.6 MB), but how much of the trunk's existing invariance reaches Berlin's fine structure is not: at 288 px the stride-16 read level becomes 18x18 (from 14x14) and stride-32 becomes 9x9 (from 7x7), so the 3x3 / 5x5 kernels of the early stages span ~1.3x less ground each and see small, survey-stable structure (street layout, building footprints, kerb lines) with more pixels, while survey-specific texture (shadow grain, canopy speckle, colour noise) is no sharper because upsampling adds no new information. Hypothesis: the limiting factor on the foreign photograph is that the trunk's scale-tuned invariance only partly engages on structures this small, and a further 1.29x enlargement engages more of it, lowering abstention without raising false fixes.
